_provenance: brms `diamonds` log-log price regression on the ggplot2 diamonds data, at N=20000. The design is the one posteriordb's `diamonds-diamonds` data file carries, rebuilt from the full 53940-row source: log(price) ~ carat * (log(x) + log(y) + log(z)) + cut + color + clarity (posteriordb models/info/diamonds.info.json), R model.matrix column order, ordered factors cut (5 levels), color (7) and clarity (8) under R's default contr.poly contrasts, giving K=25 columns: intercept, carat, log x, log y, log z, cut.L/.Q/.C/^4, color 6, clarity 7, carat:log x, carat:log y, carat:log z. Verified column by column against posterior_database/data/data/diamonds.json.zip at the 5000 rows that file uses: max |X_rebuilt - X_posteriordb| = 5.33e-15 and max |Y_rebuilt - Y_posteriordb| = 5.33e-15, which is the 15-significant-digit precision at which posteriordb stores the numbers (the posteriordb 5000 are a random, unordered sample of the full data; they were located by matching the full 25-column design row plus the response). Full data source: the ggplot2 diamonds data as distributed at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/diamonds.csv (53940 rows, md5 4d3d1d4bbad5e0806dbaec425cf90196, retrieved 2026-09-10). Row selection: Fixed-seed subsample, the house rule of real_data/README.md: numpy.random.default_rng(12345).choice(53920, 20000, replace=False), sorted, over the 53920 rows with a usable design row (20 of the 53940 rows carry a zero physical dimension and are dropped). Y = log(price) and X are the recorded regression variables; nothing is simulated. Stan's `transformed data` centering of the 24 non-intercept columns at their own column means is applied here, as models/diamonds_regression.py does at load time. init_params = DiamondsRegression.generate_init_params(1396133, k=25).
